edit_cycle_button: Create, edit or save a waveform. It does not change the currently loaded waveform.
change_cycle_setting_button: Change the waveform of the cycle sequence. The loaded sequence is plotted.
preview_canvas_widget:
Shows the whole current cycle sequence: the waveform is repeated according to the number of cycles.
 Click on the figure to enlarge.
cycle_sequence_editor:
Description of the Cycle Sequence Editor.
 
This editor is used to determine the shape of the current source. 
 - The consecutive steps determine one cycle. One step contains the duration of the set current. These steps within a cycle are repeated n times when the 'Current source app' is started. 
 - For each step, the value of the digital IO value can be set (if digital IO is enabled in the 'Settings' tab).  
 - The number of cycles is determined by the 'Cycles' field of the 'Current source app'. 
 - A preview is also shown in the app. 
 - The offset is used once before the first cycle. 
 - Press Enter after inserting a value to override the previous value. 
 - It is possible to load/save the steps from/to a JSON file.
interval_label: Time difference between two measurements. Indirectly determines the sampling rate.
average_label: The number of measurement points used for plotting a single point. The larger the value, the smoother the plotted graph.
current_start_btn: Start the 'Current source app': start the cycle sequence and if the device supports, the voltage measurement. The results are plotted in the 'Live Current/Voltage/Resistance' graph. It does not influence, not start the 'Thermometer app'. When the given cycle sequence finishes, the app stops.
current_stop_btn: Stop the 'Current source app': stop the cycle sequence and if the device supports, the voltage measurement. It does not influence, not stop the running 'Thermometer app'.
cycle_label: The number of cycles, that determines the repetition of the selected waveform.
refresh_button: Reload VISA resources. Use it when you plug the device to the computer after starting this application.
thermoprobe_label: Select the used thermoprobe. Its parameters determine the measured temperature. The parameters of the thermoprobes can be editted in 'input_files/thermoprobes.csv'.
thermometer_start_btn: Start the 'Thermometer app': start the resistance measurement and the temperature measurement based on the selected probe. The results are plotted in the 'Live Resistance/Temperature' graph. It does not influence, not start the 'Current source app'.
thermometer_stop_btn: Stop the 'Thermometer app': stop the resistance measurement and the temperature measurement. It does not influence, not stop the running 'Current source app'.
preview_start_button: Start showing the current resistance and temperature based on the selected probe. It does not plot, not save the measurement.
preview_stop_button: Start showing the current resistance and temperature.
station_start_button: Start the 'Current source app' and the 'Thermometer app' at the same time. When the given cycle sequence of the 'Current source app' finishes, both of the apps stop.
station_stop_button: Stop the 'Current source app' and the 'Thermometer app' at the same time.
raw_temp: The original data without any modifications.
compensated: This option is used for baseline correction of the original data. It subtracts the fitted 'n' degree polynomial (given by 'Polynomial Degree' input field) from the original data 'Raw Temp'.
drift: The 'n' degree polynomial (given by 'Polynomial Degree' input field) fitted to the original data 'Raw Temp'.
smoothed: Applying moving average with a window size ('Smoothing Window' input field) to the 'Compensated' data. It does not depend on the visibility of the 'Compensated' data.
transitions: Points where the data point is equal to the mean value of the data.
rise_fall_times: The time it takes for the moving averaged data ('Smoothed') to transition between two temperature values, the 10% and 90% points of its amplitude.
title: Show the title of the graph, that contains the average temperature difference, the rise and fall times calculated on the drift 'Compensated' and 'Smoothed' data.
polynomial_degree: Set the degree of the polynomial to fit on the data. It is used for baseline correction. To see this data, check 'Compensated' checkbox.
smoothing_window: Set the window size of the moving average to smooth the data. To see this data, check 'Smoothed' checkbox.
min_dist_trans: Set the minimum number of points separating two adjacent transition points. This is the minimum distance at which two transition points are considered different.
select_file_and_plot:
Select a CSV file to plot temperature data generated by the 'Thermometer app'. 
In the CSV file, each row corresponds to a data point. The first row must be: 
Timestamp   Resistance (Ohms)   Temperature (Celsius)
select_folder_and_analyze:
Save average amplitude (temperature difference), rising and falling times of the temperature measurement data from a selected folder into the 'result.csv' file. It also saves an image of the plotted data. 
Select a folder which contains the temperature measurement data. Files starting with 'log_Resistance_Temperature' are analyzed. Data is analyzed based on the settings (polynomial degree, smoothing window).
select_file:
Select a CSV file which contains the resistance data generated by the 'Thermometer app'. This data is used to (re)calculate the temperature based on the selected probe parameters. 
In the CSV file, each row corresponds to a data point. The first two values of the first row must be: 
Timestamp   Resistance (Ohms)
calibrate_button: Save the calculated temperature data into a CSV file in a format like the 'Thermometer app'.
